Solution 2 is correct. The swept area is $6\sqrt{3}+5\pi \approx 26.1003$.

**Setup.** Center the hexagon at the origin with circumradius 2: $S=(2,0)$, $A=(1,\sqrt3)$, $T=(-1,\sqrt3)$, $U=(-2,0)$, $R=(-1,-\sqrt3)$, $N=(1,-\sqrt3)$. Then $O=2S-T=(5,-\sqrt3)$. Seen from $O$, the hexagon spans angles from $\alpha_0 = 180^\circ-\arctan(\sqrt3/2)\approx139.1^\circ$ (vertex $A$) to $180^\circ$ (edge $RN$ lies on the ray from $O$ at $180^\circ$). The near boundary is $A\to S\to N$ and the far boundary is $A\to T\to U\to R\to N$. Vertices $S$ and $T$ lie on the ray at $150^\circ$, and $U$ lies on the ray at $\gamma=180^\circ-\arctan(\sqrt3/7)\approx166.1^\circ$.

**Polar decomposition.** For a direction $\varphi$ from $O$, the swept set's radial extent is the union of the hexagon's radial intervals $[a(\psi),b(\psi)]$ over $\psi\in[\varphi-45^\circ,\varphi]$. This union is an interval $[\min a,\max b]$. Here $a$ has its minimum $2\sqrt3$ at $\psi=150^\circ$ (vertex $S$), and $b$ peaks at $2\sqrt{13}$ at $\psi=\gamma$ (vertex $U$). Splitting $\varphi$ into ranges:

| Range of $\varphi$ | Radial set | Area |
|---|---|---|
| $[\alpha_0,150^\circ]$ | original slice | $\sqrt3$ (triangle $SAT$) |
| $[150^\circ,\gamma]$ | $[2\sqrt3,\ b(\varphi)]$ | $4\sqrt3-\pi+6\delta$ |
| $[\gamma,195^\circ]$ | $[2\sqrt3,\,2\sqrt{13}]$ | $\tfrac{5\pi}{3}+20\delta$ |
| $[195^\circ,\gamma+45^\circ]$ | $[a(\varphi-45^\circ),\,2\sqrt{13}]$ | $\tfrac{13\pi}{3}-26\delta-\sqrt3$ |
| $[\gamma+45^\circ,225^\circ]$ | final-position slice | $2\sqrt3$ |

Here $\delta=\arctan(\sqrt3/7)$. The $\delta$ terms cancel: $6\delta+20\delta-26\delta=0$. The $\sqrt3$ terms give $6\sqrt3$ and the $\pi$ terms give $5\pi$.

**Total:** $6\sqrt3+5\pi\approx 26.1003$.

**Other solutions.** Solution 1 gives 24 and Solution 3 gives $16+8\sqrt3\approx29.86$. Neither matches.

CHOICE: 2
